prompt.context: There is an investment company that has purchased a 12th century chateau in central France, located about a 3.5 hour drive from Paris, 1 hour from Loire Valley. The local area is primarily countryside, small villages with lots of character, lots of tourist attractions within a 1 hour drive from the castle. The castle has gone unused for ~30 years, but once refurbished will be a 6 bedroom bed & breakfast. The company is looking for 50 investors to pay $15K each to start up the business. The investors will each receive 2 weeks per year free stay at the castle as well as a 1% ownership stake in the company. You have been out of college for a few years and have managed to save a bit of money.
prompt.question: How would you go about considering whether or not to invest?

clarifying_info.q: What is the purchase price and what does the initial investment include?
clarifying_info.a: $1M purchase price, $250K renovations, $250K furnishings — total $1.5M initial investment. 50 investors x $15K = $750K equity; remaining $750K from bank debt.

Interest on debt: 10% on $750K = $75K; Proprietor salary: $40K; Landscaping: $10K ($1K/month, 50 hrs/month at $20/hr); Laundry: $10K (400 days/year x $25/day); Marketing: $10K; Breakfast: $10K (5 people x 400 days = 2,000 breakfasts x $5 each); Utilities: $5K (~$500/month); Miscellaneous: $15K (car insurance, fuel, misc. repairs). Total annual costs: $175K. Note: 400 days used to simplify math.

clarifying_info.q: What do competitors charge per night?
clarifying_info.a: Local competitors in the area: $50-$125/night; Castle B&Bs in other parts of France: $300-$500/night; Upscale hotels in Paris: $400-$500/night.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average occupancy rate in the region?
clarifying_info.a: Local tourist offices report 50% average occupancy, confirmed by key competitors.

framework: Evaluate the investment by assessing whether the Chateau will be profitable — frame as a profitability / break-even analysis
Structure financials into three components: (1) initial investment & funding, (2) annual operating costs, (3) annual revenue potential
Identify the break-even occupancy rate and compare to realistic achievable occupancy
Assess key risks that could prevent the Chateau from reaching break-even
If profitable, consider next steps / growth opportunities before making a final investment recommendation

questions.prompt: Estimate the total initial investment and how it is funded.
questions.guidance: Candidate should decompose the investment into purchase price ($1M), renovations ($250K), and furnishings ($250K) for a $1.5M total. Funding: 50 investors x $15K = $750K equity; $750K bank debt.

math.setup: Total investment = purchase price + renovations + furnishings; Equity = 50 investors x $15K; Debt = total investment - equity

questions.guidance: Candidate should identify major cost buckets first (debt service, labor, property upkeep, marketing, food, utilities, misc), then assign reasonable figures to each. Total should come to ~$175K.

math.setup: Sum all annual cost line items
steps: Breakfast: 5 guests x 400 days = 2,000 breakfasts x $5 = $10,000

questions.prompt: Estimate annual revenue potential and calculate the break-even occupancy rate. Should the investor weeks be factored in?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates set price using comparables (~$200/night is reasonable), calculate total potential room-nights (6 rooms x 400 days = 2,400), subtract the investor weeks, then solve for break-even. They should recognize that investor weeks reduce available sellable nights and ask whether 50% occupancy is achievable.

math.setup: Revenue = price/night x occupancy x sellable room-nights; Break-even occupancy = annual costs / (price x total sellable nights); Investor nights = 50 investors x 2 weeks x 7 days x (cost to chateau = $0 revenue but $1,400/week stated as value)
steps: Total potential room-nights: 6 rooms x 400 days = 2,400
Revenue at full occupancy (ignoring investor weeks): 2,400 x $200 = $480,000
Revenue at 50% occupancy (ignoring investor weeks): $240,000 — profitable vs. $175K costs
Investor weeks: 50 investors x 2 weeks x $1,400/week = $140,000 of committed value/year
Sellable room-nights after removing investor weeks: 2,400 - (50 x 14 days) = 2,400 - 700 = 1,700 (approx, across 6 rooms)
Full potential revenue from sellable nights: 1,700 x $200 = $340,000
50% of sellable potential: $170,000 — below $175K costs, essentially break-even
Key question: which 50% (% of rooms or % of available nights) is more meaningful? Regional data confirms 50% is average occupancy.
math.answer: At ~$200/night and 50% occupancy on sellable nights (~1,700), revenue is ~$170K, roughly at break-even with $175K costs. Without factoring investor weeks, 50% occupancy yields $240K — clearly profitable.

questions.prompt: What are the key risks to this investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify operational and strategic risks covering occupancy risk, execution risk, and exit risk.

questions.prompt: Suppose the chateau is doing well and returning over $100K profit per year. What should the company consider doing next?
questions.guidance: Candidate should think about organic opportunities at the existing property (pay down debt, new revenue streams) and inorganic growth (investing in additional castles). For new castles, candidate should discuss prioritization criteria such as size/economics, geography (proximity to contractors, local knowledge, marketing synergies), and customer overlap.

questions.prompt: Would you personally invest? What else would you want to know?
questions.guidance: Candidate should synthesize the profitability analysis and risk assessment into a clear recommendation. Strong candidates ask for additional information: management quality, track record of similar investments in France or other countries, survey results from target customers, and a detailed marketing plan.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key risks associated with this investment?

categories.name: Occupancy Risk
ideas: Tiny marketing budget ($10K) may be insufficient to drive awareness
Location is 3.5 hours from Paris — not easily accessible
Heavy reliance on regional tourist traffic which can be seasonal
No brand recognition as a new entrant

categories.name: Execution Risk
ideas: Timing uncertainty with French contractors for renovations
Budget overruns on renovation or furnishings
Finding and retaining a quality proprietor

categories.name: Exit / Liquidity Risk
ideas: Hard to find a buyer if the investment does not work out
Illiquid asset — a chateau in rural France is a niche market
1% ownership stake per investor makes control difficult

recommendation: At $200/night and 50% occupancy, the chateau approaches break-even (~$170K revenue vs. $175K costs) after accounting for the investor weeks that reduce sellable room-nights

The investment is marginally viable at best under base-case assumptions; meaningful upside requires either higher nightly rates (closer to Loire Valley castle comparables at $300-$500) or above-average occupancy
risks: Occupancy may not reach 50% given limited marketing budget and remote location
Renovation cost overruns or contractor delays could strain the capital structure
The investor week obligation reduces sellable inventory by ~700 room-nights per year
Illiquid investment with a narrow potential buyer pool if exit is needed
next_steps: Obtain primary data on occupancy rates from local tourist offices and direct competitor research
Develop a detailed marketing plan before committing capital
Benchmark nightly rates against Loire Valley castle B&Bs more rigorously
Understand management team's track record with similar hospitality assets
Model downside scenario at 35-40% occupancy to assess loss exposure
